title: Does Vector Quantization Fail in Spatio-Temporal Forecasting? Exploring a Differentiable Sparse Soft-Vector Quantization Approach

problem.claim: Spatio-temporal forecasting must identify subtle patterns while filtering out noise.

gap.claim: Although vector quantization has shown promise in computer vision, it falls short of improving spatio-temporal forecasting accuracy, which the authors attribute to non-differentiable optimization and the limited representation power of hard VQ.

contributions.claim: Introduces Differentiable Sparse Soft-Vector Quantization (SVQ) for spatio-temporal forecasting.
SVQ combines full differentiability, sparse-regression foundations, detail preservation, and noise reduction.
SVQ uses a two-layer MLP and an extensive codebook to reduce the computational cost of sparse regression and simplify training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On five spatio-temporal benchmark datasets, the authors report state-of-the-art results, including a 7.9% improvement on the WeatherBench-S temperature dataset.
The authors report an average mean absolute error reduction of 9.4% on Human3.6M, KTH, and KittiCaltech video prediction benchmarks.
The authors report a 17.3% improvement in image quality measured by LPIPS.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatio-temporal forecasting requires balancing subtle-pattern identification with noise filtering.
Vector quantization maps input vectors to codebook vectors or patterns and appears suited to this balance.
VQ underperforms for spatio-temporal forecasting because of non-differentiable optimization and hard-VQ representation limits.
The paper introduces SVQ, a differentiable sparse soft-vector quantization method using sparse regression, an MLP, and an extensive codebook.
The authors report state-of-the-art results and improvements across forecasting and video prediction benchmarks.
